powers.name: Move
powers.description: Move up to your Movement, hex by hex, paying each hex's terrain cost. Provokes attacks of opportunity normally.
powers.source: Universal. Every hero has this and Sidestep from the start.

powers.name: Sidestep
powers.description: Move exactly 1 hex in any direction. It provokes nothing, and the destination’s terrain cost is irrelevant — step into a hex costing 1, 2 or 3 alike. Costs no Stamina, and it is usable every other Turn. It is a bonus move, so it does NOT add your Movement stat. Paladins only.
powers.intent: The free half-step, and the drawback is the wait. On the Turn it is down you can be pinned, which is the whole reason it has a cooldown.
powers.source: 2026-08-17. Universal — every hero starts with Move and Sidestep. | 2026-08-17 : enemies have it too. This is the rule that makes zones of control soft. | 2026-08-21: Sidestep gets a cooldown of 1 — "it does break this statement of 'it's always available.' No, it's available every other turn." Enemies lose it entirely (engine/DECISIONS.md 2026-08-21: an enemy carries exactly ONE movement power in its data row). Split into two: Sidestep is free but every other Turn; Side Roll costs 1 Stamina but is always there. Rogues and Rangers take Side Roll by default, everyone else Sidestep. Beasts and Civilians get NEITHER. | 2026-08-21: "Leap. It'll move you two squares with no attacks of opportunity given. Cost 2 stamina. And give you +2 Strength until the end of your activation. And this one goes on a Warrior. And let's remove the one we gave to Priest and Mage, they both don't get one." Sidestep narrows to the Paladin — the Warrior took Leap instead, and Mage and Priest now get nothing. | 2026-08-21: the BONUS MOVE family. "Mage gets Focus. It actually does zero movement, zero stamina cost. They gain one stamina. Priest gets Devotion. Does zero movement. They lose 1 maximum stamina, and they gain 2 stamina." A bonus move IS your movement for the Activation — you pick Move, a Flight, or your bonus move, never two. "Only the full movement actions and things like them benefit from the Move stat, so all of these bonus moves do not benefit from the Move stat." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.intent: The same half-step, priced the other way round. Sidestep is free but makes you wait; Side Roll is always there and you pay for it. A Rogue who wants out every single Turn can have it, at a Stamina a Turn.

powers.name: Leap
powers.description: Move exactly 2 hexes in any direction. It provokes nothing, and the destination’s terrain cost is irrelevant. You gain +2 Strength until the end of the Turn. It costs 2 Stamina and there is no cooldown. It is a bonus move, so it does NOT add your Movement stat. Warriors only.
powers.intent: The only movement power that is an opening rather than an escape. Two hexes gets you INTO the fight and the Strength lands on the swing you take when you arrive. It rides your attacks of opportunity for the rest of the Turn too, once those exist — a Warrior who leaps into the middle punishes everything that walks past.
powers.source: 2026-08-21: "Leap. It'll move you two squares with no attacks of opportunity given. Cost 2 stamina. And give you +2 Strength until the end of your activation. And this one goes on a Warrior. And let's remove the one we gave to Priest and Mage, they both don't get one." | 2026-08-21 : "isn’t the end of activation the same as the end of this turn? I’m not trying to add one." An Activation is movement plus ONE primary action, so “until the end of your Activation” is exactly the one swing after the leap — and with attacks of opportunity unbuilt, that is behaviourally identical to end of the Turn today. Using the duration that already exists rather than adding a fifth. The two diverge once AoO is built, and end-of-Turn is the more generous reading, which suits a Warrior that just landed in the middle. | 2026-08-21: the BONUS MOVE family. "Mage gets Focus. It actually does zero movement, zero stamina cost. They gain one stamina. Priest gets Devotion. Does zero movement. They lose 1 maximum stamina, and they gain 2 stamina." powers.intent: The Mage’s bonus move is to stand still and breathe. It is the cheapest stamina in the game and the price is that you are exactly where you were — a caught caster can Focus, but it will still be caught.

powers.name: Karma decay
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Every unit in the game carries this: on kill, your Karma drops by 1.
powers.intent: Karma is the only status you spend rather than wait out. It leaves when you take a life.
powers.source: 2026-08-20: "every hero has, on kill, lower Karma by 1." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Ground layers
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE. A hex carries AT MOST ONE status, and applying a new one REMOVES AND REPLACES whatever was there — curse a burning hex to 1 Weak and the hex flips from Burn to Weak, it does not hold both. The single exception is Burn and Frost, which cancel one for one instead of replacing (rule.burn-frost-cancel): frost laid on a burning hex subtracts from it rather than swapping it. Ground layers are persistent — they carry no clock of their own.
powers.intent: The ground is a state, not a countdown. Frost put out a fire because it took the hex, not because it cancelled anything.
powers.source: 2026-08-20: "Status effects on terrain are just persistent. No turn tracking, just it is burning or it is frost. The only thing that should replace a ground layer effect is if a different one is applied, it replaces the previous one. The ground can only have one effect on it, and that effect stays." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | Ruled 2026-09-02. Verbatim: "All ground effects, remove and replace, except Burn and Frost which counter. So if i curse a ground to add 1 weak, but it had burn. It flips from Burn to Weak. So each ground tile can only have 1 status on it."

powers.name: Summon order
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Every summoned unit is given a summon number when it arrives — the first thing summoned is 1, the second is 2, and so on, counted separately for each side. In its own Phase, summoned units activate FIRST, in summon-number order, BEFORE any unit that was already on the field. Summoned heroes go first in the Hero Phase; summoned enemies go first in the Enemy Phase.
powers.intent: A summon that arrives and then waits behind everything else is a summon that did nothing. Going first is most of what you paid for.
powers.source: 2026-08-20. Written ahead of the summoning system itself, which does not exist yet — see engine/COMBAT-SEQUENCE.md #Summoning. | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Enemy attacks are defined, and melee is the floor
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Every enemy states its attacks explicitly, by attack id — an enemy with no attack listed is unfinished content, not an enemy that cannot swing. If an enemy has no melee attack among them, it carries attack.basic.melee: Strength +0, melee reach, no stamina. A ranged enemy still has it, for when something closes.
powers.intent: Nothing on the board is ever unable to act. A caster shoved into melee swings for Strength; it does not stand there empty-handed.
powers.source: 2026-08-30: "every enemy needs its attacks clearly defined. If it does not have a melee attack, an enemy has a basic melee S+0 damage attack." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Nothing outlasts the Battle
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. No effect in the game persists past the end of the Battle — not a stat change, not a status, not a drain, not a scar. The longest any effect can last is the rest of the Battle, which is the first of the four durations. "Permanent" in any entry means permanent WITHIN the Battle and nothing more; an effect that would carry into the next Battle does not exist.
powers.intent: The Battle is the unit of consequence. A hero who ends one drained is whole at the start of the next, and content never has to reason about state it cannot see.
powers.source: 2026-08-31: "There's no permanent past the end of battle for anything." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: A status magnitude is a value
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Any status a unit is carrying may be read as a NUMBER by damage or by another effect — "Strength + 2 x the target's Root" is legal, and so is scaling a duration, a heal or a chance off a status the target already has. This holds for every status, not a named few.
powers.intent: It gives every status a second life. A debuff you applied three Phases ago is still worth something because the next attack reads it.
powers.source: 2026-09-01: "All of them or status effects can also be used to change the scale of damage or effect." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Forced movement is Knockback and Pull
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. There are exactly THREE forced-movement verbs: Knockback, which pushes a unit directly away from the source; Pull, which draws it directly toward the source; and DRIVE, which is a Knockback in which THE ATTACKER ALSO MOVES FORWARD — the target is pushed and the attacker advances into the hex it left. All three take a number of hexes and all three run on ONE axis: nothing moves sideways. No fourth verb.
powers.intent: Two opposed verbs, one axis. The 2026-08-20 cut left only Knockback because Pull had arrived as a bespoke system for one power; reinstated 2026-09-01 as a first-class verb with a real roster behind it.
powers.source: 2026-09-01: "Yep, I'm adding pull back in. It's a reversal." Reverses the 2026-08-20 ruling "the pull is cut. Knockback is the only forced movement in the game." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | 2026-09-01: the 'no third verb' clause is SUPERSEDED. Drive added, verbatim: 'Drive is knockback, but the attacker also moves forward.'

powers.name: Limits stop stacking; options need no limit
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. The per-unit limits on Armor, Idols, Blood Runes and Relics exist for ONE reason: to stop every item slot being additive in the same direction. A hero may not wear five defensive things. Trinkets carry no such limit because a trinket gives an OPTION — a thing you can do — not a bigger number, so five of them buy five choices rather than five stacks. The authoring test is therefore: if it is additive it belongs in a limited category; if it is an option it can be a trinket. The one deliberate exception is a status IMMUNITY, which is additive but conditional: it is often worth nothing, so its value is the pre-battle question of who should carry it today. That is a War Council decision, not a stack, and immunities stay trinkets.
powers.intent: It makes item slots a COVERAGE budget rather than a power budget. Handing a hero another slot makes them more flexible, not stronger — which is why slots can grow generously without inflating anything.
powers.source: 2026-09-02: "The reason for the Idol, Blood Rune / Armor / Relic limits are to prevent EVERY item slot from being additive in any direction. So I can't just add 5 defensive things. Because the Trinkets mostly give options, they don't need that limit." And on the exception: "I intentionally had immunities as an exception, because they are useless often, [I] want it in planning. OK, I can use my immunity — on whom? Is a good, non-permanent choice in battle prep." | Merged onto the trunk from the parallel chat 2026-09-02; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling.

powers.name: All healing comes from one function
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. There is ONE heal in the game and every source routes through it — a power, an item, a trigger, a lifesteal rider, and REGENERATION, which does not heal by a private path of its own but calls the same function at End of Phase. Anything that modifies healing therefore modifies all of it, once, in one place: Karma raises the amount, Burn halves it. Content never has to say which kinds of healing it means, because there is only one kind.
powers.intent: It turns three special cases into one pipeline. Karma boosting heals, Burn halving them and Regeneration ticking are not three rules that happen to touch health — they are stations on a single function, and a new modifier is written once instead of per source.
powers.source: 2026-09-02: "Regeneration should CAUSE healing, healing should all come from same function." Answers the open question from the healing-cures-Bleed decision: Regeneration IS healing received, so everything true of a heal is true of a Regeneration tick. | Merged onto the trunk from the parallel chat 2026-09-02; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling.

powers.name: Burn and Frost cancel
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE. Burn and Frost annihilate each other one for one, at the moment either is applied — a unit never carries both. Apply 2 Burn to a unit holding 1 Frost and it ends on 1 Burn; apply 1 Frost to that unit and it ends on 0. The same cancellation is the ONE exception to ground layers replacing each other (rule.ground-layers).
powers.intent: Fire and ice are the only pair in the game that argue instead of taking turns.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02. Verbatim: "Do you have a note that Frost and Burn counter each other. Add 2 burn to a target with 1 Frost, you end up with 1 Burn. Add a frost to that unit and you end up with 0."

items.description: Immunity to Frost 1. One point of Frost is removed BEFORE Frost resolves, so that point never gets to increase the physical damage you take. The ordinary -1 decay still follows, so Frost falls by 2 a Turn.
items.intent: One point of Immunity makes you substantially immune to the thing. That is the whole item.
items.source: Settled content, 2026-08-17 — rebuilt on 's Immunity mechanic (was written as a plain End-of-Activation strip, which is half of it). | 2026-08-17 corrected: immunity resolves BEFORE the status does; it is not a second strip. The status still takes its own -1 afterwards.

items.name: Lumberjack's Axe
items.intent: A working tool that has stopped asking what it is for. The first two-handed axe in the game, and it belongs to a civilian.

attacks.name: Punch
attacks.intent: The attack EVERY PLAYER UNIT has — ruled 2026-08-25, confirming the 2026-08-22 Brawler ruling. Universal: no kit grants it and no row lists it, because a per-row flag would be a second source for one fact. Brawler reads its brawl tag. Damage soft.
attacks.source: authored 2026-08-25 — the universal punch the Brawler ruling required | RE-RULED 2026-08-27, verbatim: "Every single classed hero, the six classes, is supposed to have the attack punch. It does strength - 1 damage. Cost: 0 stamina. Has -5 to hit and -5 crit. It is a brawl attack and a melee attack." Stamina 1 -> 0, and the -5/-5 are new. Civilians keep Punch by their own dictated stat blocks; this ruling names the six classes.

attacks.name: Cleave
attacks.targets: an adjacent hex and one hex adjacent to both you and it
attacks.source: dictated 2026-08-25 (Lumberjack) — attack 2 hexes; the two-hex sweep shape already exists

attacks.name: Basic Attack
attacks.source: 2026-08-30: "every enemy needs its attacks clearly defined. If it does not have a melee attack, an enemy has a basic melee S+0 damage attack." The floor every enemy stands on: Strength +0, no stamina, no accuracy modifier, one target in melee reach. An enemy that was never given a melee attack has this one.

statuses.name: Karma
statuses.effect: While you carry Karma: every heal you receive is increased by your Karma, and every point of damage you deal is increased by HALF your Karma, rounded down.
statuses.decay: NONE. Karma has no tick-down at End of Activation and there is no decrease-Karma stage in Settling at all. The −1 resolves inside the onKill settle that the killing damage starts. Because nothing decrements it on the clock, Karma has no ordering constraint in Settling — ruled 2026-09-02: "its order doesn't matter."
statuses.source: 2026-08-20. The only status that decays on an event rather than on the clock. RE-RULED IDENTICALLY 2026-08-25, verbatim: "Karma increases healing and increases damage by half of the Karma value. So it increases healing to the target that has karma by the amount of karma. And one half of the Karma value is added to all damage. Karma is lost whenever the unit kills another unit. So, every unit, during player attack, if there is a kill, there is a check to see if there is karma, and if there is, it goes down by one." | Ruled 2026-09-02. Verbatim: "Karma does not tick down at end of activation, so ACTUALLY its order doesn't matter. There is no decrease Karma stage during settling. That should happen during the onKill settling from damage."

statuses.name: Slow
statuses.effect: While you carry Slow, your Movement is reduced by your Slow.
statuses.decay: -1 at End of Phase, like Burn, Poison, Bleed, Weak, Stun and Frost.
statuses.source: 2026-08-20: "clean up that movement stuff." Fourteen entries said "the target loses N Movement on its next Turn" — one meaning, two wordings, and the only per-target clock left in the game. It is a status now, so it decays on the same ladder as everything else and nothing has to remember whose next Turn it is. | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

statuses.name: Taunt
statuses.effect: Cuts both ways by who applied it. A HERO taunting an enemy makes that hero the enemy's priority target in AI selection while the Taunt lasts — the enemy fixates. An ENEMY taunting a hero takes the hero away from the player: it becomes AI-driven, activates FIRST in the Hero Phase, prioritises the unit that taunted it, and the rest of the party acts afterwards.
statuses.decay: -1 at End of Phase, like Burn, Poison, Bleed, Weak, Stun, Frost and Slow.
statuses.source: 2026-09-01: "Taunt takes hero control away from the player when it's used by an enemy. Taunt, when used by a hero, makes the enemy fixate on the hero." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

statuses.name: Dazed
statuses.effect: The player loses control of the hero for as long as it lasts. Unlike Taunt there is no priority target — the unit simply behaves as the AI would drive its striker type.
statuses.decay: -1 at End of Phase, like Burn, Poison, Bleed, Weak, Stun, Frost and Slow.
statuses.source: 2026-09-01: "Dazed, used on a hero, causes the player to lose control of it, the same as a taunt, for a number of turns... it just means the player loses control and the unit is going to behave the way it would in the simulation with the AI for that striker type." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

statuses.name: Confusion
statuses.effect: Inflicted on an enemy, it swaps that enemy's AI strategy for a different one while it lasts.
statuses.decay: -1 at End of Phase, like Burn, Poison, Bleed, Weak, Stun, Frost and Slow.
statuses.source: 2026-09-01: "Confusion inflicted on an enemy causes it to use a different AI strategy." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

statuses.name: Root
statuses.effect: While you carry Root you CANNOT MOVE AT ALL — not a reduction, a stop. Movement actions and bonus moves alike are unavailable for as long as it lasts.
statuses.decay: -1 at End of Phase, like Burn, Poison, Bleed, Weak, Stun, Frost and Slow.
statuses.source: 2026-09-01: "Root means cannot move at all. For its duration. It takes down one per turn, like other statuses." Root also has a customer that scales off its magnitude (the Spider's Chomp), which rule.status-as-a-value makes legal. | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

statuses.name: Bleed
statuses.effect: N TRUE damage at End of Phase, then −1. True damage, so neither Armor nor Resist touches it — that is what "Bleed is never resisted" always meant, now said in one word.
statuses.decay: −1 at End of Phase, the shared clock.
statuses.curedBy: Healing received removes Bleed equal to HALF the healing (rounded nearest, 0.5 up). Regeneration is healing (rule.one-healing-function), so a Regeneration tick strips Bleed too. Burn halves healing received first, so the Bleed removal is half of what actually landed — a burning unit sheds a quarter of what it otherwise would.
statuses.source: Ruled 2026-09-02. Verbatim: "Bleed is True Damage." and "Bleed is being converted to magnitude damage. Also healing should cure bleed. Regen should be healing." SUPERSEDES the old flat model (N was a turn count, each tick a flat 2). This also closes the standing "does Armor touch Bleed?" question: it does not — nothing does.

statuses.name: Frost
statuses.effect: A unit carrying Frost N takes +N on EVERY physical hit it receives — all physical, melee and ranged alike, and PER HIT: a two-swing attack against Frost 3 takes +3 on each swing, +6 in total. Frost deals no damage of its own; it is the mirror of Armor, which subtracts from the same number. Bleed beats Resist by being true; Frost beats Armor by outgrowing it.
statuses.decay: -1 at End of Phase, the shared clock. Frost carries no ordering constraint in Settling — ruled 2026-09-02 that its tick-down order does not matter, and it may go first.
statuses.application: Applied like Burn. Burn and Frost annihilate one for one on application (rule.burn-frost-cancel) — a unit never carries both.
statuses.source: RULED 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'Frost should ADD to physical damage. Then its order of ticking down in settling also doesn't matter, but it can go first.' and 'Frost is applied like Burn.' Direction (incoming), scope (all physical, not melee only) and per-hit application ruled the same day. Ends the two-week gap in which content referenced Frost with no definition.

statuses.name: Shadow
statuses.effect: Shadow does nothing on its own. It TICKS UP — first of everything in Settling — and is then compared to the unit's Max Health. The moment Shadow is AT OR ABOVE Max Health the unit is OBLITERATED: killed, removed from the field, and NO CORPSE is left. It is the only effect in the game that denies a corpse, which is what makes it worth fearing rather than merely surviving.
statuses.decay: NONE — it is the one status that grows. +1 per Settle, and it never falls on its own clock.
statuses.source: RULED 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'Shadow, ticks UP during settling (first), then is compared to max health. If shadow = max health, unit is obliterated. (killed, removed from field, no corpse).' Tick size (+1) and the at-or-above threshold ruled the same day. Shadow was named 2026-09-01 with no effect anywhere — this is its first definition, and the last unshaped status is now shaped.

testCohort.note: Ruled 2026-08-20: the standard engine test party — six heroes, one per class, COPIED from live Codex heroes so they can be tweaked without touching the originals. Clearly differentiated: test- typeIds, (TEST) names, never ships. The engine reads these through the generated pack (mkenginepack.mjs) — nothing hand-typed engine-side. Testing-lane riders travel on the cohort and retire one by one as published sources land; the Sky Pirate's own Cutlass bleed already retires test.ranger.serrated-arrows.
testCohort._movesNote: moves are derived from the class bonusMove in gen/classes.json, ruled 2026-08-21: Warrior Leap, Rogue/Ranger Side Roll, Paladin Sidestep, Mage Focus, Priest Devotion, Civilian/Beast none. Corrected 2026-08-21 - the cohort had been carrying the pre-rebuild assignment where nearly everyone got Sidestep. audit.mjs enforces the match, so restoring the old values will fail the build.
testCohort._copyOfNote: Lucius and Osric were tutorial heroes. The tutorial path was cut 2026-08-21 - its 96 rows were 24 heroes duplicated across their own level art - so they now copy the eve-base heroes that own those pictures. The cohort still covers six classes.

alphaTeam.note: THE ALPHA TEAM, dictated 2026-08-27: "take those heroes and make them the way they are supposed to actually be in content" — the test cohort rebuilt on the real scaffolding. Same stat bodies (copied from testCohort, which copied live heroes 2026-08-20), one hero per class, but armed through kit -> authored items -> authored attack rows instead of the engine's six PROVISIONAL attacks. Test-only statuses translated into the vocabulary: ward->protection, hobble->slow, enfeeble->weak. Punch arrives via universalToAllUnits, never listed. Movement powers are derived from class by the converter. Clearly differentiated: alpha- typeIds, (ALPHA) names, never ships. Arcane Bolt is NOT carried over — the Air Mage's ability is now the Lightning Staff's, as a real item grant.

critChart.note: RULED DATA, NOT A CONTENT KIND (decided 2026-08-27, closing the question parked 2026-08-09). One copy, here; COMBAT-DESIGN.md crit section is the design authority and this block mirrors it. The chart never produces an injury.* badge — battle-only, cleared at battle end; permanence is the Deathbed pipeline alone. Resolution: normal damage always lands; cup.crit-branch flips a coin — heads +50% damage BEFORE Armor/Resist/Protection, tails cup.crit-effect rolls evenly among the rows. One chart for all damage types, fully symmetric. Entry point name fixed in GLOSSARY.md: rollCritEffect. Row keys exist so event-log lines can name their cause (Law 12) — keys, not content ids.

branch.heads: +50% damage, applied before Armor, Resist and Protection

critChart.source: Six rows 2026-08-09 (extracted from GAME-DESIGN §4); four added by ruling 2026-08-27 (Knocked Sprawling, Winded, Guard Broken, Nerve Struck) — every axis covered: stamina, mitigation, the body.

durations.note: RULED 2026-09-01, verbatim: 'Until end of next activation, or 2 activations, is correct.' The four Turn-worded durations are SUPERSEDED. An Activation is the unit-specific window (the totality of one unit's doing of things); a Turn is not. Everything battle-scoped is written in Activations or in the Battle.

list.name: until the end of your Activation
until the end of your next Activation
list.note: the default carry — survives the enemy phase and one more of yours

list.name: for the rest of the Battle

durations.source: Ruled 2026-09-01, closing the duration question both handoffs left open.

statusFamilies.note: Named 2026-09-02, and the Bleed conversion is what made the split clean. MAGNITUDE: N is how much. DURATION: N is how long — and that family is forced, because "cannot move" has no magnitude. Bleed was never an inconsistency; it was a magnitude status wearing a duration number, and it has been moved to the family it belonged in. rule.status-as-a-value reads a status's number either way — the family says what the number means.
